channel.title: The Dig — NISQ algorithms
channel.description: Papers relevant to operating, benchmarking, integrating and using a semiconductor spin-qubit quantum computer of at least 16 qubits that is co-located with and integrated into an HPC system. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the NISQ algorithms preset. Today’s ranked reading list centers on silicon spin-qubit hardware and operational benchmarking: 2611.12850 proposes over-gate TiN stressors to enhance valley splitting in Si/SiGe wiggle-well dots, 2611.14114 offers a cloud-executed GHZ-fidelity benchmark that tests whether calibration data predict processor performance, and 2611.12217 maps how multi-dot configurations affect electron temperature and double-dot latching for initialization and readout. The skim-tier items broaden the context but sit further from current spin-qubit operation: 2611.13301 presents an MLIR-based fault-tolerant compiler, 2611.12779 a neutral-atom arbitrary two-qubit gate architecture, 2611.13371 silicon-spin qLDPC syndrome extraction with mobile ancillas, 2611.14422 a QRAM energetic-cost accounting method, and 2611.13796 an analog Rydberg-atom QAOA MaxCut study.
